issues.t: Ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off while driving, often after a bump or if the key ring is heavy. Power steering and power brakes are lost, and the airbags may not deploy in a crash.
issues.why: The original ignition switch needs too little force to turn out of Run. This is the well-known GM ignition switch recall 14V-047.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls now. Until it is fixed, use only the key itself with nothing else on the ring. If it stalls, grip the wheel firmly, brake hard and steer to safety.

issues.t: Power steering assist cuts out (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, especially at low speed or when parking, often with a power steering warning message. It may come and go.
issues.why: The electric power steering motor on the steering column can fail. GM recalled these cars under 10V-073 to replace the motor.
issues.next: Steering still works, but takes much more effort, so slow down and allow more room. Check your VIN for the free repair before paying for one.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Off (recall)
issues.sym: The key comes out of the ignition while it isn't fully off, and the car can roll away if it isn't in Park or the parking brake isn't set.
issues.why: Worn or out-of-spec ignition lock cylinders let the key be pulled early. Covered by recall 14V-171.
issues.next: Always put the car in Park (or in gear with the brake set for a manual) before taking the key out. Check your VIN for the free lock cylinder replacement.

issues.t: Fuel pump module can crack and leak gas (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gas smell, especially after filling up, or fuel wetness near the top of the tank.
issues.why: The plastic fuel pump module on top of the tank can crack and let fuel escape. Covered by recalls 09V-419 and 12V-459.
issues.next: If you smell gas, don't drive or park in a closed garage. Check your VIN and get the free repair.

issues.t: Aftermarket ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving on a car that had its ignition switch replaced with a service part.
issues.why: Some replacement ignition switches sold for repairs had the same weak design as the original. Covered by equipment recall 14E-021.
issues.next: If your switch was replaced before 2014, ask a dealer to confirm it is the corrected part. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

issues.t: Shifter may show Park when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The gear display says Park but the car is actually in another gear. It may not restart, or it may roll after you get out.
issues.why: A shift lever indicator fault on some automatic cars. Covered by recall 09V-073.
issues.next: Set the parking brake every time you park. Check your VIN for the free repair.

issues.t: Front lower control arm bushings wear out
issues.sym: Clunking or rattling from the front over bumps and cracks, or a clunk when you accelerate. Steering may feel loose.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front lower control arms tear or separate early, sometimes before 35,000 miles. It is the most reported G5 complaint.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. Most shops replace the whole control arm because the bushing is not sold separately outside the dealer.

issues.t: Sway bar end links clunk
issues.sym: A light knocking or clunk from the front when going over small bumps or driveway ramps.
issues.why: The small links connecting the sway bar to the suspension wear out. Owners report it as the most common G5 repair on TrueDelta.
issues.next: Not urgent, but have the front suspension checked so a worn control arm or strut isn't missed. End links are a simple repair.

issues.t: Front struts fail early
issues.sym: A bouncy or floaty ride, knocking over bumps, or oil on the strut body.
issues.why: Owners report front struts wearing out around 30,000–40,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the struts and mounts checked. Replace them in pairs and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Rusted fuel lines leak gas
issues.sym: A strong gas smell, fuel dripping under the car, or the fuel level dropping fast.
issues.why: The steel fuel lines under the car rust through, especially where roads are salted. Owners report it from about 56,000 miles.
issues.next: Don't drive with a fuel leak; it is a fire risk. Have the car towed and the corroded lines replaced.

issues.t: Key gets stuck or won't turn in the ignition
issues.sym: The key won't turn back to remove it, or it is stuck in Run. The battery can drain if the car can't be shut off.
issues.why: A failing park switch in the automatic shifter can keep the key locked in. A worn lock cylinder causes the same thing.
issues.next: Make sure the shifter is fully in Park and wiggle it. If that doesn't release the key, have the shifter switch and lock cylinder checked.

issues.t: Check engine light from cam timing solenoid or sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with cam timing codes, sometimes with poor acceleration or rough running.
issues.why: The solenoids that control the variable cam timing, and the cam position sensors, fail on these engines. Low or dirty oil makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. Have the codes read; a solenoid or sensor is a fairly simple fix, but repeated codes can point to timing chain wear.

issues.t: Water pump or thermostat failure and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant leaks, a low growl from the engine, heater going cold, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: Owners report water pumps failing under 40,000 miles and thermostats being replaced on several model years.
issues.next: If the gauge goes toward hot, pull over and shut the engine off. Check coolant when cool and have the system pressure tested.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch and rattle
issues.sym: Rattling at idle, misfires, check engine light or a no-start. One owner's chain failed and the car was scrapped.
issues.why: The timing chain and its tensioner wear, especially when the oil is low or changed late. These are interference engines, so a jumped chain can bend valves.
issues.next: Have any new rattle checked promptly. Keep the oil full and changed on time.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing noise from the engine that is loudest on a cold start, sometimes with an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The exhaust manifold cracks from repeated heating and cooling. Owners report it around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Exhaust leaks near the engine can let fumes into the cabin. Have it inspected and repaired soon.

issues.t: Check engine light from the gas cap
issues.sym: Check engine light or a check gas cap message, usually soon after filling up.
issues.why: A loose or worn gas cap lets fuel vapor escape and the emissions system flags a leak.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light stays on after a few drives, replace the cap and have codes read.

issues.t: Steering column or shaft clunk
issues.sym: A clunk or pop felt in the steering wheel when turning, especially at low speed.
issues.why: Wear in the steering shaft or column. Owners list it among the most common G5 repairs.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft and column checked. Ask whether recall work on the power steering has been done.

issues.t: Wheel bearing humming
issues.sym: A hum or growl that gets louder with speed and may change when you turn.
issues.why: A worn wheel bearing or hub assembly.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed soon. A badly worn bearing can get hot and affect steering and braking.

issues.t: Turn signal stalk or chime stops working
issues.sym: Turn signals won't cancel or don't work, or the turn signal clicking sound goes silent.
issues.why: The turn signal stalk wears out. The clicking sound is made electronically, and owners report it going silent along with other chimes and the radio.
issues.next: Signals must work for safety, so have the stalk and circuits checked. If only the sound is gone, check the cluster and radio.

issues.t: Radio stops working
issues.sym: The radio goes dead or stops working, sometimes along with door chimes.
issues.why: Owners report factory radio failures around 45,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the radio fuse first. A used or rebuilt radio is an option besides a new one.

issues.t: Reduced Engine Power warning from throttle body
issues.sym: A Reduced Engine Power message, the car won't accelerate normally, and the check engine light is on.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body or its sensor fails, and the computer limits power to protect you.
issues.next: Get to a safe spot; restarting may clear it for a while. Have the codes read and the throttle body checked.
